note: Every deliberate hard case, registered before it is drawn. `handle` is filled by the generator with the live handle of the trap's own entity in arch.dxf (validate: every trap resolves). `expected` is the product behaviour the trap tests. The conventions are learned from real Dhaka architectural sets; no geometry, text, name or number of any real set is carried.

traps.expected: the label writes a nominal whole-feet size (18'-0" x 14'-0") against a clear 17'-10" x 14'-2": a label is a cross-check, flagged, never a quantity; the room's geometry governs

the typical door schedule prints D-2 as 08 NOS against nine D2 tags placed per floor: a declared disagreement that refuses the D2 count and the faces D2 opens onto until a person states the quantity (L-MEA-02)
the guard room's rear wall lines stop 60 mm short of its east wall: the room is not closed as drawn and defers SURFACE_NOT_CLOSED, never bounding-boxed (L-MEA-03); a person closes it with S-Measure
TOILET-02's label stands outside the toilet with a leader to it: the leader, not the label's insertion point, names the room
both flats label a room BED-01 (and KITCHEN, LIVING, ...): a name is not an identity; the two rooms are two objects keyed by where they stand
the east flat's doors are the west's door blocks inserted mirrored (x scale -1): one block, two hands, both read as the same door type
the study's door is drawn exploded (a LINE leaf and an ARC swing, no INSERT): a learn-and-count by block finds one fewer D2 than the schedule and the tags; the gap in the wall is the door

the kitchen louvre V-2 is 1'-0" x 1'-0" (0.093 m²): not over 0.1 m², so it is retained in the kitchen's faces and the duct wall's brickwork and listed, never deducted (L-MEA-02); the toilet ventilator V-1 (0.139 m²) is deducted
a 5'-0" gap with no leaf in the dining / living partition (drawn with the beam over it dashed): wider than 4'-0", so LIVING and DINING are one space carrying two labels, measured once
bed, sofa and dining-table blocks and a closed rug outline stand inside rooms: none is a wall, a room outline or an opening
one wall face line is drawn twice, stacked: a wall is one pair of faces, never two walls
columns are closed outlines filled with a solid hatch, standing across the wall lines: a column is an obstruction inside the room's wall-face outline, never a wall and never a room boundary
room sizes are written in feet-inches (17'-8" x 5'-8") on a millimetre drawing: the notation is read in its own unit and cross-checked against the geometry
the lift core's shear walls are drawn as double lines 250 apart (200 from 3F), hatched as concrete: a thickness-only wall reader must not mint BW250 brickwork from the RCC core
the plan tags a door D2 (circled, unhyphenated) and the schedule spells it D-2: one mark in two spellings
the wall-type table is captioned WALL TYPES (no SCHEDULE, LEGEND or PLAN word): at this tranche's HEAD the caption grammar reads it UNTYPED; ARCH-3 teaches the grammar TYPES
